Nitpicks: The agent’s presentation/formatting (numbered list, including the URL) is fine and does not affect usefulness. Also, reporting rights as “Public Domain” while the page may show it in more than one place/with an additional language line is acceptable as long as the stated wording is exactly displayed somewhere.

Critical issues: The identifier is wrong and not supported by the DOM evidence. The agent reported “90402/SK-A-2344” (hyphenated), but the only evidenced identifier-like string is the record path in the URL “90402/SK_A_2344” (underscore). Moreover, the DOM snapshots do not show any on-page field explicitly labeled “Identifier,” so the agent could not have faithfully copied an identifier “as displayed” from the visible record content; instead it appears to have inferred or reformatted it. This violates the hard constraint to preserve the identifier exactly and to use the identifier from the exact record as displayed.

What was done correctly: The agent did use the exact Europeana record page (DOM shows https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/90402/SK_A_2344 and “The Milkmaid | Europeana”). Title “The Milkmaid,” creation date “2013,” providing institution “Rijksmuseum,” type “painting,” and rights “Public Domain” are all directly supported by the DOM text on that page.

Outcome assessment: Because the task’s stopping condition and primary deliverable require recording all six requested fields exactly from the record, and one of those six (identifier) is incorrect/unsupported, the agent did not successfully complete the task as asked, despite getting the other five fields right.
